strengths: Well-motivated problem reformulation from MDP to POMDP perspective, clearly articulating the limitation of frame-independent processing in VLA models
Comprehensive experimental validation spanning simulation (LIBERO 4-suite, CALVIN) and real-world robot tasks (Mobile ALOHA) with consistent improvements across benchmarks
Thorough ablation studies isolating contributions of AVA module and state initialization, demonstrating each component's value (Tables 3-5)
Strong empirical results: 98.0% average SR on LIBERO (vs 96.8% baseline), 4.65 avg length on CALVIN (vs 4.28 baseline), with robust performance under perturbations
Effective qualitative visualizations (Figures 4-10) providing interpretable evidence of task-relevant attention focusing on critical visual features
Successful real-world demonstration on physical Mobile ALOHA robot showing practical applicability beyond simulation
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: AVA module uses standard components (MLPs, self-attention, FFN); recurrent state formulation lacks formal theoretical justification for belief state approximation

Missing critical comparison with other history-modeling baselines: no comparison with Transformer-based temporal encoding, other RNN variants, or sequential visual encoders—a fundamental gap given the core contribution
No computational cost analysis: inference time overhead of recurrent computation not quantified; token pruning requires 50-60% retention to maintain performance, limiting practical benefits
Incomplete hyperparameter justification: T=4 frame sequence chosen for computational feasibility without ablation; L2 regularization weight appears ad-hoc; initial state r^{-1}=0 arbitrary
Real-world evaluation scale limited: only 30 trials for Mobile ALOHA (10 per object) vs thousands in simulation; 4 tasks tested—insufficient for statistical significance assessment
Incremental improvements in several settings: LIBERO single-task 99.2% vs 99.0% baseline; CALVIN shows marginal gains on some tasks—typical improvements are 1-2 percentage points
Missing failure analysis and error characterization: no discussion of when historical context is insufficient or method underperforms relative to baselines
Attention mechanism design choices underexplored: custom mask excluding language/instruction tokens from modulation lacks justification; FiLM modulation not compared with alternatives

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Clearly identifies and addresses the limitation of VLA models processing frames independently, with sound POMDP-based theoretical grounding
Comprehensive experimental validation: Consistent improvements across three benchmarks (LIBERO, CALVIN, Mobile ALOHA) with thorough ablation studies (Tables 4-7) demonstrating component effectiveness
Rigorous ablation design: Tables 4-7 effectively isolate contributions and control for confounding factors like training compute, with matched training settings comparison
Insightful behavioral analysis: Figure 4 visualization of attention dynamics and Figures 7-11 showing learned focus patterns across viewpoints provide good interpretability
Clear presentation and reproducibility: Well-structured paper with detailed implementation details, comprehensive appendices, open-source base models, and good figure quality
Practical efficiency: LoRA-based optimization keeps parameter overhead <1% of base model
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: The AVA module uses standard components (MLPs, cross-attention, softmax). While the application to recurrent VLA is novel, the mechanism itself is relatively straightforward
Incremental improvements: CALVIN shows modest gains (98.2% vs 97.5%), LIBERO task-specific benefits vary significantly; 1-2% gains on several tasks may not justify added complexity

Incomplete computational analysis: No FLOPs or latency measurements reported; recurrent processing overhead not quantified; memory requirements for hidden states not analyzed; implications for real-time control unclear

Severely limited real-world validation: Only 4 Mobile ALOHA tasks with 30 demonstrations each; no real-world baseline comparisons; claims of 'real-world applicability' unsupported; all long-horizon results remain simulation-based

Hyperparameter tuning concerns: Different penalty coefficients for different benchmarks (c=0.2 for LIBERO, c=0.1 for CALVIN); state initialization provides minimal ablation benefit (97.4% vs 97.2%) yet is task-specifically enabled

Insufficient design analysis: No systematic study of history length; missing sensitivity analysis for key hyperparameters; no investigation of whether attention captures temporal dependencies vs. static features

Loose POMDP connection: While conceptually motivated, the connection between theoretical POMDP formulation (Eqs. 3-4) and actual attention mechanism is tenuous; POMDP serves more as post-hoc motivation than derivation foundation

Limited failure mode analysis: Figure 13 failure cases attributed to 'spatial belief errors' without deep investigation; no systematic study of when/why attention mechanism fails or whether it helps in failure scenarios
Temporal grounding not addressed: Method doesn't explicitly encode timestep information; unclear how model distinguishes recent vs. distant history in recurrent state
